documents.note: The bare HDFC is held by two directory entries, so a directory alone cannot settle it; the document does, through the debit row's HDFC Bank and its HDFC IFSC.
Each row starts with its IFSC and ends with its account. The first account is three characters from the second row's IFSC and 49 from its own, so only the row says which code is its own.

documents.note: Each short name is held by two directory entries and nothing else in the note settles it, so the right answer is no organisation, with the directory on or off.
The salary account is tied to its bank only by the IFSC beside it; the bank is never named.
The directory has no French bank codes, so the IBAN is tied by the BIC on the next line. The domestic bank code, branch code and account are the IBAN's own parts.
The collection account is tied to its bank only by the IFSC beside it; the bank is never named.
HDFC Ltd has the match key of the bare name HDFC, which two directory entries hold; the full name on the next line, whose initials it is, settles it as the mortgage company.
A visa page, not a passport: its dates are the visa's. The passport number on it is the holder's current passport, which is another document.

passport.why: The machine-readable zone fails its expiry check digit and gives 14 May 2031; the printed date is 15 Apr 2031. Both are after the reference date, so the passport is current either way.
